m:katedra: The square can be seen for free at any time. The cathedral can be visited outside services; I couldn't find the exact hours or the price of the crypt and bell tower on an official website: check the Go Vilnius page (govilnius.lt) or at the door.
m:gediminas: Open every day from 10am to 8pm, ticket office closes half an hour earlier (National Museum of Lithuania website, lnm.lt). Ticket €8, reduced €4; the «Historic Triangle» with the Castellan's House and the Old Arsenal costs €15. On the last Sunday of the month entry is free for all. Walk up in about 10 minutes, on wooden steps that are slippery in rain or frost, or take the funicular (€3 return, €2 one way, 10am–8pm): one guide notes it was stopped for works in 2025, so check it's running. Closed on 1 and 2 November and 24 and 25 December.
m:valdovu: From September to May: Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10am–6pm, Thursday 10am–8pm, Sunday 10am–4pm; closed on Mondays. Last entry is an hour before closing (official website valdovurumai.lt). You buy one route at a time: they cost from €4 to €10 each, all four €17, with up to 50% off additional routes. On the last Sunday of the month entry is free. Closed on 1 November and from 24 to 26 December.
m:pilies: Free to walk at any time. The restaurants on Pilies street are for tourists and cost more than those on the side streets; to eat better, turn into Stiklių gatvė or Šv. Mikalojaus gatvė.
m:univ: Courtyards: Monday–Saturday 9am–6pm; St John's Church Monday–Saturday 9am–7pm, Sunday 9am–3pm; bell tower every day 10am–7pm with tickets until 6:30pm (university museum website, muziejus.vu.lt, undated page: to be confirmed). Bell tower ticket €7 (€4 reduced). The entrance is on the Universiteto gatvė side.
m:aurora: Chapel: every day 6am–7pm from May to October, 7am–7pm from November to April; St Teresa's Church Monday–Saturday 10am–7pm, Sunday 7am–7pm (Go Vilnius). Entry is free. It's a place of prayer: the street below the chapel is full of worshippers, so pass through quietly.
m:anne: Entry is free, but opening hours inside are limited and I couldn't find them on an official website: if it's closed, the façade can be seen from outside at any time. It photographs best in the morning.
m:uzupis: Free to walk at any time. The «Užupis» passport stamp costs a few euros. To eat there are cafés and bars on the riverside.
m:hales: The market is open Tuesday to Saturday 7am–6pm and Sunday 7am–3pm (official Go Vilnius listing, from 2024); Monday isn't listed and it's probably closed: check. Individual stalls have their own hours, usually from 9–10am to 4–5pm.
m:kgb: Wednesday–Saturday 10am–6pm, Sunday 10am–5pm; closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, and on national holidays (govilnius.lt). Ticket €6, reduced €3. The route through the cells is harrowing and not suitable for small children.
m:croci: The park is always open and free. The climb from Cathedral Square takes about 15 minutes; the path is steep and can be slippery in rain or ice, so wear good shoes.
vd:lokys: A restaurant in a brick-vaulted cellar off Pilies street, specialising in Lithuanian cooking with game and traditional dishes: cold beetroot soup (šaltibarščiai), cepelinai, grilled meat and local beer.
vp:lokys: Upper-mid range in the listing (three symbols out of four). Soups cost €8–9 (Wolt menu): for a main course allow €15–22 (estimate). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:snekutis: A traditional Lithuanian restaurant on a quiet street in the centre: cepelinai, potato pancakes (bulviniai blynai), soups and meat with potatoes, in simple rooms and at an unhurried pace.
vp:snekutis: Mid-range (two symbols out of four in the listing). Menu not read: roughly €10–16 a dish (estimate). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:trobele: A Lithuanian tavern just outside the Old Town, popular with locals: cepelinai with curd cheese, potato dumplings with spinach, linseed bread baked daily and a honey liqueur (Žalgiris balsam).
vp:trobele: Mid-range (two symbols out of four in the listing). Menu not read: roughly €9–15 a dish (estimate). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:uzupio: The riverside café-restaurant at the entrance to Užupis, next to the bridge and the mermaid: simple Lithuanian cooking, soups, salads and cakes, with a view of the river.
vp:uzupio: Mid-range (two symbols out of four in the listing). Menu not read: roughly €8–15 a meal (estimate). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:mint: A café with a bookshop on an inner street of the Old Town: homemade cakes, vegan snacks and mint tea. A quiet place to stop with a book.
vp:mint: Budget (one symbol out of four in the listing). A tea with a slice of cake costs roughly €5–8 (estimate). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:bagel: A small bagel shop in the historic Jewish quarter, near the Pylimo Jewish museum: lox bagels, bialys and other Jewish baked goods. For a quick meal or to take with you.
vp:bagel: Budget (one symbol out of four in the listing). A salmon bagel is roughly €5–8 (estimate). Closed on Saturdays and Sundays; by the afternoon everything's gone. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:hales: Inside the Halės covered market: a counter of freshly roasted coffee for breakfast and Smoke House with pastrami sandwiches and other hot dishes, to eat standing or at the market tables.
vp:hales: Budget (one symbol out of four for the market bistro in the listing). A coffee and a sandwich are roughly €8–12 (estimate). On Mondays the market is probably closed. Hours from the official 2024 Go Vilnius listing, to be confirmed.
vd:rosehip: A vegan bistro in the centre, between the Old Town and Gedimino avenue: soups, bowls and veggie burgers with local produce. A light break between stops.
vp:rosehip: Mid-range (two symbols out of four in the listing). A dish is roughly €9–14 (estimate). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:nazionale: Lithuania's history from the Middle Ages to today, in the arsenal.
cd:mo: Lithuanian contemporary art, in a Daniel Libeskind building.
cd:ebreivilna: The history of the Jews of Vilnius, the «Jerusalem of the North».
cd:torretvvilnius: Lithuania's tallest tower, with a revolving restaurant.
cx:torretvvilnius: It's about 5 km from the centre.
cd:ambra: Baltic amber with fossil insects and jewellery.
